subject: Feature costing & unit-econ qualification for PriHealth
messages:
From: Amanda Lowe <amanda@prihealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 01, 2027 at 15:12 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — PriHealth 'patient triage' feature

Ben / Marissa — thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can align procurement and finance quickly: 

Call recap (high level)
- Feature: 'patient triage' (automated symptom intake + suggested next step) to be added to our patient portal.
- Expected pilot footprint: 200k monthly active users (pilot cohort / early rollout), average ~3 feature calls per MAU per month.
- Avg tokens per call (round-trip, prompt + response + context) ~200 tokens.
- That implies ~120M tokens / month (200k * 3 * 200).

Budget & targets
- Finance gave a guideline budget range for the first 6 months: $6k — $15k / month (flexible depending on outcome).
- Procurement needs a clear target $ / 1M tokens and a $ / feature estimate to plug into our unit economics model.
- Our growth team wants CAC payback <= 9 months if possible.

Asks for you (Ben / Redwood):
1) Provide a simple banded pricing suggestion for $ / 1M tokens (pilot, growth, scale tiers) and the math showing how that maps to $ / feature given our token assumptions.
2) A short memo on your expected minimum gross margin vs inference cost (we understand there will be enterprise discounts) — we need to show this internally for procurement.
3) An editable spreadsheet with a worked example (tokens -> $ / month -> $ / feature -> impact to CAC payback) we can share internally.

Attaching our procurement worksheet and a quick token-projection CSV. Please treat these as internal.

Attachments: prihealth-procurement-sheet.xlsx; prihealth-token-projections.csv

I can loop in Tom from procurement (cc in next email) to get procurement cadence moving. Can you aim to send the pricing memo + workbook by EOD Thursday (Apr 2)?

Thanks — Amanda
Amanda Lowe
Head of Product Operations, PriHealth
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Lowe <amanda@prihealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 02, 2027 at 09:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — PriHealth 'patient triage' feature

Amanda — appreciate the clear recap. We ran the numbers off your assumptions and attached a short template that walks through 3 pricing bands and the $/feature conversion. High-level summary below; the workbook (attached) has line-item math you can plug into your models.

Quick answers (baseline assumptions)
- Assumed traffic: 120M tokens / month (per your projection).
- Assumed average tokens / feature call: 200 tokens -> ~5,000 feature calls per 1M tokens.

Suggested customer-facing bands (examples)
- Pilot band (0–30M tokens/month): $25 / 1M tokens (introductory price, limited term).
- Growth band (30–100M tokens/month): $45 / 1M tokens.
- Scale band (100M+ tokens/month): $35 / 1M tokens (volume discount).

$ / feature mapping (illustrative)
- At $45 / 1M tokens: $/feature = $45 / 5,000 = $0.009 per feature (roughly $0.01).
- At $35 / 1M tokens: $/feature ≈ $0.007.

Cost & margin context (high level, more detail in workbook)
- Typical Redwood incremental inference cost (hardware + ops) in production-optimized runs: ~ $7 / 1M tokens (this is a platform-level baseline; subject to model/quantization).
- That implies gross margin (before enterprise discounts / support) of ~ 80–85% at the $35–45 / 1M list bands. For enterprise deals we expect to land in the 60–70% gross margin range after structured discounts.

CAC payback framing
- Using your budget floor ($6k/mo) and the $45 / 1M example: 120M tokens -> $5400/month at $45/1M. With that spend, $/feature ~ $0.009.
- To evaluate CAC payback we need the following inputs from you: expected ARPU contribution per converted user (monthly), incremental conversion attributable to the feature, and average customer lifetime / retention. With conservative assumptions we can usually show a 6–9 month payback for self-serve driven features; enterprise sales-led flows typically run longer.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Attached: redwood-feature-econ-template.xlsx — editable workbook with the calculations above.
2) Marissa / Grace: can one of you run a short sensitivity with Amanda's ARPU and conversion lifts to give a proposed discount/commit that hits PriHealth's CAC payback target?
3) Schedule: propose a pricing+procurement sync Apr 6 (30 minutes) to align on SOW / trial cap. Amanda — is Apr 6 at 10am PT good?

Attachments: redwood-feature-econ-template.xlsx

Thanks,

Subject: PriHealth — unit-econ deep-dive & mutual action plan (internal)

Marissa / Grace — summary and proposed internal asks following Amanda's confirmation. This is internal: do not share the cost baseline text with the customer verbatim (we disclose margins carefully in enterprise discussions).

Key inputs from PriHealth
- Traffic: 120M tokens / month (200k MAU * 3 calls * 200 tokens).
- Budget: $6k — $15k / month.
- Procurement wants a 3-month pilot: 30M token cap at pilot band, then transition to growth band.

Illustrative unit-econ math (customer-facing examples we can show)
- Tokens / 1M -> features per 1M = 1,000,000 / 200 = 5,000 features.
- At $45 / 1M tokens: cost to customer = $45 * 120 = $5,400 / month -> $/feature ≈ $5,400 / 600,000 = $0.009.
- At $35 / 1M tokens (scale): cost to customer = $4,200 / month -> $/feature ≈ $0.007.

Redwood unit cost (internal baseline)
- Platform incremental inference cost: ~ $7 / 1M tokens.
- If customer pays $45 / 1M -> gross margin (before discounting support / on-call / custom infra) ≈ (45 - 7)/45 ≈ 84%. For deal sizing, assume we may need to concede to 60–70% gross margin after enterprise concessions.

CAC payback example (high level)
- Using the $45 / 1M scenario and the $6k/mo spend: we need Amanda's ARPU/conversion delta to model payback precisely.
- Action: Marissa — can you run 3 sensitivity cases in the attached workbook (best/likely/worst) using these spend levels and show the discount or committed term required to achieve <= 9 month payback?

Proposed commercial approach
1) 3-month pilot: 30M cap at $25 / 1M (introductory).
2) Auto-transition to Growth band: $45 / 1M up to 100M.
3) Negotiated scale step: $35 / 1M at 100M+ (annual commit).
4) Offer a PO-friendly SOW with a defined success metric (conversion lift or handle-rate improvement) to trigger a discount extension.

Action items (owners)
- Marissa: run CAC-payback sensitivity (adds to workbook) — due Apr 6 EOD.
- Grace: draft pilot SOW language + pilot success metrics (due Apr 7).
- Ben: prepare slide for Apr 6 pricing sync and confirm Apr 6 10am PT meeting with Amanda / Tom.

Attachments referenced: redwood-feature-econ-template.xlsx; prihealth-token-projections.csv
